cards.text: This is the last stretch of Psalm 119, and the writer is still talking straight to the LORD. No warm-up, either: "I call with all my heart; answer me, O LORD! I will obey Your statutes."

cards.question: He calls to the LORD again and asks to be saved, so that he may ___ God's testimonies.

cards.text: This man rises before dawn to cry for help. Before DAWN, friend. Me? I'd hit snooze on the sun.

cards.question: Up before dawn and crying for help. Where does the writer say he has put his hope?
The writer says his eyes anticipate the watches of night. What for?

answers.text: To keep watch over the city

cards.text: He asks the LORD to hear his voice and give him life. Then he says people who follow after wickedness are drawing near, and friend, that is NOT the crowd you want pulling up a chair.

cards.question: The people who follow after wickedness are close to God's law.
With wicked people drawing near, the writer tells the LORD that He is ___.
The writer only learned recently that God established His testimonies forever.

cards.text: New stretch, same man, same heart. He asks the LORD to look upon his affliction and rescue him.

cards.question: The writer wants the LORD to rescue him. What reason does he give?

answers.text: He has not forgotten God's law
He was born in God's land

cards.text: Then he says, "Defend my cause and redeem me; revive me according to Your word." Friend, that's a man handing God his whole case file.

cards.question: The writer says salvation is far from the wicked because they do not seek God's statutes.

cards.text: Then he tells the LORD His mercies are great, and asks again to be revived. But his persecutors and foes? There are a LOT of them.

cards.question: With so many persecutors and foes against him, the writer has turned from God's testimonies.

cards.text: He doesn't hide how he feels about the faithless, either. He looks on them with loathing because they do not keep God's word.

cards.question: The writer asks the LORD to consider something about him. What is it?
How much of God's word does the writer call truth?

cards.text: And he says all God's righteous judgments endure forever. Not till Tuesday. Not till the warranty runs out. FOREVER.
Here comes the final stretch of the whole psalm. Rulers are persecuting the writer, and he says it's without cause.

cards.question: With rulers persecuting him, the writer says his heart fears the rulers.
The writer rejoices in God's promise. What picture does he use for that joy?

answers.text: Someone who wins a long race

cards.text: Great spoil. That's the face you make finding cash in an old coat pocket, times a THOUSAND. And he says it plain: he hates and abhors falsehood, but God's law he loves.

cards.question: How many times a day does the writer praise God for His righteous judgments?

cards.text: SEVEN times a day. Friend, I check the oven seven times before the first batch even goes in, so I know it's possible. Then he turns to those who love God's law: abundant peace belongs to them.

cards.question: The writer says those who love God's law can still be made to stumble.

cards.text: He waits for God's salvation, and he carries out God's commandments. He obeys God's testimonies and loves them greatly.

cards.question: The writer obeys God's precepts and testimonies, and he says it's because all his ways are before God.

cards.text: He's bringing it home now. Twice he asks that his cry and his plea come before the LORD.

cards.question: When the writer asks for his cry to come before the LORD, what does he ask to be given?
The writer says his lips pour forth praise because God teaches him His statutes.

cards.text: His tongue sings of God's word too, because all God's commandments are righteous. Then he asks for God's hand to be ready to help him.

cards.question: The writer wants God's hand ready to help him. His reason: he has ___ God's precepts.

cards.text: Then the writer says, "I long for Your salvation, O LORD, and Your law is my delight." Longing and delight in the same breath. Friend, this man is ALL in.

cards.question: The writer asks the LORD to let him live. Live to do what?
In the last verse of the psalm, what does the writer say about himself?

answers.text: He has strayed like a lost sheep
He has stood like a strong tower
He has run like a swift deer

cards.text: So he asks the LORD to seek His servant, for he has not forgotten God's commandments. A lost sheep asking to be found. What a way to end 176 verses.

findings.problem: The question begins with "He calls to the LORD" without identifying who "He" is. With the opening story card no longer on screen, the pronoun depends on context the baker cannot see; the question should identify the writer.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what.
